attachments.content:
Create a high-fidelity, polished design. Follow this general design process (use the todo list to remember): (1) ask questions, (2) find existing UI kits and collect design context — copy ALL relevant components and read ALL relevant examples; ask the user if you can't find them, (3) start your file with assumptions + context + design reasoning (as if you are a junior designer and the user is your manager), with placeholders for the designs, and show it to the user early, (4) build out the designs and show the user again ASAP; append some next steps, (5) use your tools to check, verify and iterate on the design. Good hi-fi designs do not start from scratch — they are rooted in existing design context. Ask the user to Import their codebase, or find a suitable UI kit / design resources, or ask for screenshots of existing UI. You MUST spend time trying to acquire design context, including components. If you cannot find them, ask the user for them. In the Import menu, they can link a local codebase, provide screenshots or Figma links; they can also link another project. Mocking a full product from scratch is a LAST RESORT and will lead to poor design. If stuck, try listing design assets and ls'ing design system files — be proactive! Some designs may need multiple design systems — get them all. Use the starter components (device frames and the like) to get high-quality scaffolding for free. When showing multiple design options on one page, decide between (a) a single full-size responsive prototype with a tweaks panel, or (b) a vertical stack of anchored option cards. Choose based on how design-y vs prototype-y the ask is, how many options there are, and how big each is. For (b): Present multiple design options as a vertical stack of turns — each turn of options is its own `
`, newest turn at the **top**, and every option gets a stable `{turn}{letter}` id (`1a`, `1b`, `2a`…) that the user references back in chat and you cross-link between turns. Always include `` in `` — the host provides pan/zoom, so the user can freely zoom out on designs wider than the viewport. **How to write it** — put one `
2Riffs on 1b
2aTighter spacing
…design…
…

Try next: "more like 2a but with the serif from 1c" · "make 2b full-bleed" · "new directions"

…turn 1, unchanged…
``` **Rules:** turn section ids are `t1`, `t2`, `t3`…; option ids are `1a`, `1b`, `2a`… and go on the option's **outermost** element (`.dv-opt`), never on the badge — so `#1b` scrolls the whole option into view. Ids are stable forever, never reused or renumbered. Options within a turn sit side-by-side in a wrapping row; don't hand-roll your own pan/zoom — the host canvas provides it. **Every** option-id reference in the file — turn heading, option label, `.dv-next` line, any prose — is an `1b` link, never a bare `1b`; in your chat replies, just write `1b`. End each turn with a one-line `.dv-next` of 2–3 plain-English follow-ups the user could paste into chat. Size each `.dv-card` to its content (explicit width is fine); don't use `height:100%`. When designing, asking many good questions is ESSENTIAL. Give options: try to give 3+ variations across several dimensions. Mix by-the-book designs that match existing patterns with new and novel interactions, including interesting layouts, metaphors, and visual styles. Have some options that use color or advanced CSS; some with iconography and some without. Start your variations basic and get more advanced and creative as you go! Try remixing the brand assets and visual DNA in interesting ways — play with scale, fills, texture, visual rhythm, layering, novel layouts, type treatments. The goal is not the perfect option; it's exploring atomic variations the user can mix and match. CSS, HTML, JS and SVG are amazing. Users often don't know what they can do. Surprise the user. If you do not have an icon, asset or component, draw a placeholder: in hi-fi design, a placeholder is better than a bad attempt at the real thing.

<design-system-guide>
# Opportunity Designed — Design System

Brand + product design system for **Opportunity Designed**, a solo strategic
consultancy founded by **Addie Morrow** (Salt Lake City, UT). The practice helps
consumer brands and the retailers that sell them find and capture growth —
buying, merchandising, category strategy, operations, and market access.

> Opportunity doesn't appear. It's built.
> See what others miss.
> **Opportunity. Designed.**

This repo is the single source of truth for the brand's typography, color,
visual motifs, reusable UI components, and full-screen recreations of the
marketing website.

---

## Sources used to build this system

Everything here was reconstructed from materials the client provided:

- **Marketing website HTML** — `index.html`, `about.html`, `contact.html`,
  `opportunity-review.html` (production pages for opportunitydesigned.com).
  These carried the structure, inline styles, class vocabulary, and copy.
- **Brand + Marketing Playbook** (`BRAINSTORM EDITS OpportunityDesigned_Brand_Marketing_Playbook.docx`)
  — the master voice/tone guide. Extracted to `research/playbook.txt`.
- **Logo & mark library** (`README.txt` + ~40 PNG/SVG marks) — the stipple mark
  in black / white / violet / parchment on every surface, plus favicon/app-icon
  sizes. Copied into `assets/`.
- **Fonts** — Anton (display) and Inter 300–700 (body), provided as woff2.
- **Headshots** of Addie Morrow (`headshot*.jpeg`).
- **Business document templates** (`.docx`): Proposal, Cover Letter, Timeline &
  Scope, Master Services Agreement, Mutual NDA, Invoice, Rate Card, Discovery
  Call Guide, Client Onboarding Packet, Fill-In Guide. Content references for
  future document templates.

### ⚠ Known gap / caveat
The website's compiled CSS (`css/index.css`, `css/about.css`, etc.) and
`js/site.js` were **NOT** provided — only the HTML that links them. Exact
numeric values (paddings, transition timings, some type sizes) are therefore
**reconstructed** from the inline styles, class names, README colors, and font
files, not read from source. They are faithful but not byte-exact. **If you can
share the site CSS, the UI-kit fidelity will tighten considerably.**

Note also: the mark library's `README.txt` is headed "THE STRATEGY STUDIO" — an
internal file name. The public brand is **Opportunity Designed**; "The Studio"
is the name of the *methodology*, not the company.

---

## CONTENT FUNDAMENTALS — how the brand writes

The voice in one word: **Precise.** Calm, controlled, terse. The operator who
already sees the move and doesn't announce it. Dry authority that doesn't
justify itself.

**Point of view.** First person singular — **"I"**, not "we". This is one
person: "I've been the buyer." "I close the gap between who you are and where
you're going." The client is addressed as **"you"**.

**Casing.** Sentence case for headlines and body — *never* default Title Case.
Eyebrows, section labels, figure codes, and meta are **UPPERCASE, letter-spaced**
("ABOUT", "01 — WHO I AM"). The playbook explicitly favors all-caps or lowercase
over Title Case. Instagram register goes lowercase for a human feel.

**Sentence shape.** Short. Declarative. Fragments are fine and encouraged.
"Operator first, consultant second." "Say the thing. Don't explain the thing."
No throat-clearing, no preamble, says it once.

**Structure.** Three-line brand arc (problem → truth → outcome):
*"Lost in everyone else's noise. Found in who you are. / Who you are is the
strategy. Where you go is by design. / Opportunity. Designed."*

**Emoji:** none. Not part of the brand. (The playbook uses an ℹ glyph only as an
internal editorial note marker — not in customer-facing copy.)

**Numbers & proof** are stated flatly, no hype: "10+ years", "35+ brands",
"National placements incl. Ulta, Costco, Target, Whole Foods."

**Words to own:** design · designed · by design · opportunity · gap · noise ·
precision · momentum · niche · foundation · clarity · operator · margin · the
buy · the seat.

**Words to avoid (banned):** fractional, inflection, optimize/optimization,
synergy, solutions, disrupt/disruptive, leverage (verb), holistic, robust,
stakeholder (client-facing), best-in-class, value-add, impactful, circle back,
gut check.

**Right vs. wrong** (from the playbook):
- ✗ "We leverage synergistic frameworks to optimize your brand's growth trajectory."
- ✓ "I close the gap between who you are and where you're going."
- ✗ "As a fractional executive… I bring a holistic approach."
- ✓ "I've been the buyer. I know what it takes to get the yes."

**Reference brands for register:** Satisfy Running (technical specs as poetry),
gnuhr_studio, Berghain — earned, raw, no explanation needed.

---

## VISUAL FOUNDATIONS

The system reads like an **architect's / engineer's drawing sheet** — a
technical, blueprint sensibility applied to a warm, earthy palette. Restraint is
the point; white space is authority, not emptiness.

**Color.** Two brand surfaces: **Parchment** `#F7F2E8` (warm off-white, the
default) and **Obsidian** `#1C1916` (warm near-black). One accent only —
**Violet** `#5C4A82` on light, lightening to `#B49CE0` on dark and for links.
**Dusk** `#8A7D6E` is the muted/secondary text taupe. No second accent, max two
background tones per surface. The palette is deliberately warm and near-mono;
violet is used sparingly, as a "moment of precision and light."

**Type.** Display is **Anton** — condensed, single-weight, tight leading
(`line-height ~0.98`), sentence case for hero statements, uppercase for labels.
Body is **Inter, light-forward** — 300 is the brand's default body weight, with
500–700 reserved for emphasis. Big Anton headline + delicate Inter 300 body is
the signature tension: "technical/clinical meets handwritten/informal."

**Layout.** Wide architectural margins (`--mx: clamp(20px,6vw,120px)`).
Sections are numbered (`01`, `02`…) with an uppercase title and a top hairline
rule — like sheet sections. Content is often two-column: a big left statement,
a smaller right paragraph. A drafting **title-block** sits in the footer
(Project / Drawn by / Discipline / Sheet 01 of 03 / Scale 1:1 / Rev A).

**Signature motifs:**
- **Corner registration ticks** — L-shaped marks in the four corners of a
  "plate" (content panel). Class `.tk .tl/.tr/.bl/.br`. Reproduced as the
  `Plate` component.
- **Figure captions** — "Fig. 01 · A. Morrow" under images, and inline "Fig. 01"
  labels on grid cells. Photos are treated as plates/figures.
- **Grain overlay** — a full-viewport low-opacity film grain (`--grain-opacity`
  ~0.05) over everything, for a printed/analog feel.
- **The mark** — a stipple/pointillist blob read three ways: *cloud* (see what
  others miss), *inkblot* (value what others overlook), *fingerprint* (own what's
  yours). Used at 3 rotations.

**Backgrounds.** Flat parchment or flat obsidian — no gradients, no photographic
hero washes except one duotone mountain image on the homepage. Texture comes
from grain, not color. Section backgrounds alternate parchment ↔ a `.paper`
(slightly lighter) ↔ obsidian for rhythm.

**Borders & cards.** Hairline rules (1px, low-opacity warm ink) do most of the
structural work. Cards are near-square (radius 2–8px, mostly ≤4px), flat or with
a very soft warm shadow (`--shadow-md`). No rounded-pill cards, no colored
left-border accent cards. The "plate" with corner ticks is the brand's card, not
a drop-shadowed box.

**Radii.** Nearly square everywhere — 2px default, 4px common, 8px max. Pills
only for small status chips.

**Shadows.** Sparse and warm-tinted (`rgba(28,25,22,·)`). Most elevation is
communicated by hairlines and surface tone, not shadow.

**Motion.** Calm and controlled — **no bounce, no spring**. Fades and short
translate-ups on scroll, `--ease-out` (0.22,1,0.36,1), 140–480ms. "The operator
who already sees the move and doesn't announce it" applies to motion too.

**Hover / press.**
- Buttons: filled → darken to `--violet-deep`; outline → fill with ink/violet.
  Text links → underline offset grows, color shifts to violet.
- Press: subtle — a 1px downward nudge or slight opacity, never a big shrink.
- Focus: `--shadow-focus` violet ring.

**Transparency & blur:** minimal. Used only for the sticky nav (a faint
parchment/obsidian scrim on scroll) and the grain layer. No frosted-glass
everywhere.

**Imagery vibe:** warm, grainy, unposed — mid-motion, from behind, or intimate
detail; drama from light vs. dark, not styling. Salt Lake City / Wasatch terrain
is on-brand. Headshots are the main provided imagery.

---

## ICONOGRAPHY

The brand is **icon-light by design** — it favors *typographic* markers over a
glyph set. Where most systems reach for an icon, this one uses:

- **Numerals** — section numbers (`01`–`04`), figure codes ("Fig. 02a"), and
  ordered lists carry the visual rhythm.
- **Corner registration ticks** — the drafting-sheet L-marks (drawn with CSS
  borders, not an icon font) are the closest thing to a repeated "icon."
- **A few Unicode glyphs**, used deliberately and sparingly: `→` (arrow, in
  CTAs and "read more"), `↑` (back-to-top), `·`/`—` (meta separators), `✓`
  (form success), `☰` (mobile menu). No decorative emoji, ever.
- **The stipple mark** is the brand's only illustrative asset, used as
  logo/figure — not as a UI icon.

**Recommendation for product/app surfaces that genuinely need icons** (e.g. a
client portal): use **Lucide** (`lucide.dev`) at 1.5px stroke — its thin,
precise, geometric line style matches the technical register. It is loaded from
CDN in the UI kit where needed and flagged there. This is a *substitution* — the
provided sources contain **no icon set of their own**; do not treat Lucide as
canonical brand iconography without sign-off.

Marks & icons live in `assets/` (mark on every surface + favicon/app-icon sizes).
The provided `README.txt` in the mark library is the authoritative "which mark
where" guide; its logic is reproduced in the Brand cards.

---

## Index / manifest

**Foundations & entry**
- `styles.css` — global entry (import this). `@import`s the four token files.
- `tokens/colors.css` · `tokens/typography.css` · `tokens/fonts.css` · `tokens/layout.css`
- `readme.md` (this file) · `SKILL.md` (Agent-Skill wrapper) · `thumbnail.html`

**Assets** — `assets/` : `logo.svg`, mark PNGs (black/white/violet/parchment on
each surface), favicon/app-icon sizes, `headshot*.jpeg`, `fonts/`.

**Foundation specimen cards** — `guidelines/` (Colors, Type, Spacing, Brand).

**Components** — `components/` (see each dir's `.prompt.md`):
- `core/` — Button, ButtonText, Eyebrow, SectionHead, Plate, FigCaption,
  Tag, TitleBlock, Field, GrainOverlay.

**UI kits** — `ui_kits/`:
- `website/` — recreation of the Opportunity Designed marketing site
  (home, about, opportunity-review, contact).

**Slides** — `slides/` — branded 16:9 deck templates (title, statement, service
pillars, case study, quote, closing).

**Research** — `research/playbook.txt` (extracted brand voice guide).

</design-system-guide>
